content: The overall loss to follow-up (LTFU) rate was 4%, with 26% in the intervention arm and 50% in the control arm. Several domains of bias risk were classified as unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. Each trial had more than three domains with high or unclear risk of bias. The meta-analysis showed a high degree of heterogeneity (I² = 95%, 91%-97%). The effects observed in individual randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were consistently beneficial, and no differences were noted in other critical outcomes. The Guideline Development Group (GDG) determined that downgrading for inconsistency was unnecessary, and no downgrading was performed. The original sample size did not represent the effective cluster-adjusted sample size in the meta-analysis. In the meta-analysis, studies such as Choko (2019a) with multiple intervention arms using similar HIV self-testing (HIVST) kit distribution methods had their arms combined. However, studies like Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), which also had multiple intervention arms with different HIVST kit distribution methods, did not have their arms combined. Adjustments were made to the control arm sample to prevent double counting. Choko (2019b) included two intervention arms and two subgroups (antenatal care [ANC] women and antiretroviral therapy [ART] clients). The HIVST arms were combined, but the subgroups were presented separately. Cluster-adjusted analyses were included for cluster-randomized trials. Ten individual RCTs and seven cluster-randomized trials were included. Downgrading was performed once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in all trials. Attrition bias was noted in one trial (Patel, 2018), which had an overall LTFU rate of 36%, with 44% in the intervention arm and 27% in the control arm. Recruitment bias was present in three cluster-randomized trials. Several domains of bias risk were unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. The meta-analysis of Wray (2018) combined intervention arms with similar HIVST kit distribution methods. Four individual RCTs and two cluster-randomized trials were included. Downgrading was performed twice due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in all trials. Recruitment bias was noted in one cluster-randomized trial, and unclear risk of bias for selection bias (allocation concealment), selective reporting, and baseline cluster imbalance was identified in another. The meta-analysis of Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017) included only one arm involving direct distribution of HIVST kits to peers compared to the standard of care. Two cluster-randomized trials were included. Downgrading was performed once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in both trials. The meta-analysis of Choko (2019b) included only the ART group. One individual RCT and one cluster-randomized trial were included. Downgrading was performed twice due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in both trials. Recruitment bias was noted in the cluster-randomized trial, and all trials had more than three domains with high or unclear risk of bias. The meta-analysis of Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017) included only one arm with facility-based HIVST distribution compared to the standard of care. Three cluster-randomized trials were included.
